text: For every pair of real numbers k and h, if k ≥ 2, h ≥ 0, and h ≤ 1/4, then both inequalities k/2 ≤ k(k + h + 1)/(2k + h) and k(k + h + 1)/(2k + h) ≤ (4/5)k hold. The same universally quantified k and h occur throughout the hypotheses and both conclusions. All arithmetic and ordering are over the real numbers. Real division is totalized, with division by zero defined, but the hypotheses imply 2k + h ≥ 4 > 0; hence the variable denominator in these conclusions is strictly positive. The fixed numerical denominators 2, 4, and 5 are also positive. Every displayed constant is an absolute numerical constant independent of k and h. There are no existentially chosen constants, additional parameters, or further assumptions.
domains: k and h are real numbers; all operations and comparisons are over ℝ.
quantifiers: Universally quantified k and h, implicit binders in the Lean statement.
scopes: Both universal quantifiers scope over all three successive hypotheses and the entire conjunction. All three hypotheses jointly imply both inequalities.
constant_dependencies: All constants are fixed numerical constants; none depend on k or h.
